destination.name: Ronde Lutherse Kerk (Koepelkerk)
destination.note: No installed model or landmarks.json entry covered this pand (Oude Lutherse Kerk is a different church, Singel 411). Jan Roodenpoortstoren is demolished (1829) and was skipped.

facts: Round domed church by Adriaan Dortsman, 1668-1671 (Lutherans were forbidden a tower, so a dome with a small lantern carrying the Lutheran swan was built).
Burnt 18 Sept 1822, only the walls survived; rebuilt 1823-1826 to plans of T.F. Suys and Jan de Greef with a raised dome and Roman coffers.
Dome fire 3 Feb 1993, restored by June 1994; the roof is copper-coloured, no longer green.
Register 2207: round domed church in classicist forms with a 'zijbeuk' built against the rear half; copper roof.

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012179368, ground 0.461 m NAP, roofMax 43.3 m NAP; wall to 24.5-26.4 m at the drum, dome planes 27 to 34.7 m, lantern 34.7 to about 43; annex roofs 17.4-20.4 m; north-east tail roofs 8-12 m.
measuredBy.geometry: Circle fitted to the exposed BAG arc: centre (-3.0, -3.5) native m from the footprint centroid (4.8937841, 52.3779083), radius 13.16 m (model R 13.3). Nine window bays of 40 degrees centred on bearings 237 + 40k read from ref-west.jpg (camera about 276 degrees).
uncertain: Window bay phase (+-5 degrees) and the lower-tier window sizes are read from one oblique photograph.

The annex (zijbeuk) and the low houses at the north-east tail have no photographs; they are the BAG polygon extruded to the 3DBAG roof height with flat tops and no openings (audit blank-wall warnings are expected and left alone).
The 2025 municipal panoramas show the drum under scaffolding and sheeting and could not be used for detail.
